incident-bot: ALERT kv-cache pool us-west-2 under memory pressure and continuous-batching surge. p95 generation latency x4, some pods OOM killed. alert: https://grafana.internal/d/kv/alerts?id=9876

Samir (oncall): taking pager. calling trace link + qlen histo. Does anyone recall changes to continuous_batcher or batching thresholds in the last 30m? @jess @lee

Jess: I rolled a change 22m ago to KV_AUTOTUNE=true with increased window sizing for batching. It was to improve throughput but I see now the rollout hit us. Rolling that change back immediately.

Lee: reproducing logs: repeated "CUDA out of memory" when allocator attempts cudaMalloc with small slices. PyTorch arena keeps growing, fragmentation_ratio high. Continuous_batcher holds onto kv handles across micro-batches.

Samir (oncall): list of impacted pods: kv-cache-prod-7a, kv-cache-prod-7b, kv-cache-prod-7c, kv-cache-prod-7d. Dumping python tracemalloc + nvprof on kv-cache-prod-7b now.

Jess: rollback command issued:

```
kubectl -n prod set env deploy/kv-cache KV_AUTOTUNE=false KV_BATCH_WINDOW_MS=25
kubectl rollout restart deploy/kv-cache
```

OpsBot: Rollout started for deployment/kv-cache uid=rb-2026-06-02-17 status=progressing

Lee: applied temporary allocator tuning configmap:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  arena_compact_threshold: "0.3"
  small_slab_limit: "24MB"
  compaction_interval_seconds: "45"
```

Samir (oncall): also reduced KV_BATCH_MAX_CONCURRENCY to 6 for the pool via hotpatch to reduce peak coalescing.

Marco: customer-impact: 4 enterprise accounts experienced timeouts and degraded throughput for ~18 minutes. Estimated affected requests ~1.8k, highest impact on model-serving endpoints for personalized features. CSMs alerted and we sent a short outage notice.

Samir (oncall): immediate results: after rollback and restarts memory RSS decreased ~35% and fragment_ratio metric dropped from 0.82 to 0.48 within 7 minutes. p95 latency trending down but some 502/504s for draining requests.

Lee: Root-cause hypothesis: autotune increased micro-batch window size, increasing KV entry lifetimes and creating many transient small allocations in GPU memory. PyTorch allocator not reclaiming small slabs quickly -> fragmentation -> cudaMalloc fails -> OOMs. Continuous batching code also held references longer than expected in certain error paths.

Samir (oncall): mitigation checklist completed -> rollback applied, concurrency cap set, allocator compaction increased, pod restarts initiated. Next steps for RCA:
- instrument continuous_batcher to log outstanding kv refs per request
- add unit/regression test simulating high coalescence to CI
- evaluate switching small-slab allocation strategy or embedding jemalloc/TCMalloc
- consider a safe-guard in autotune to bound KV entry lifetime and memory per host

Marco: I'll own customer comms and schedule RCA doc. Handing monitoring and follow-up to Lee for next shift at 02:30 UTC. Leaving runbook pointer: https://wiki.redwood.internal/ops/kv-cache-memory

Samir (oncall): handing to Lee. I'm available for questions. closing pager if stable.

incident-bot: RESOLVED alert kv-cache memory surge in us-west-2 at 1754005678
